thread:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - GPU pool 'us-west2-gpu-pool' at 100% capacity (available: 0). Pending pods: 18. Autoscaler status: no scale-up (quota or constraints).

alice: Copy, seeing infra-bot alert. Who's triaging?

bob: On it. Pulling pending list now.

bob: `kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | grep Pending` -> large chunk are from job batch-train-2026-03-18, 14 Pending, nodeSelector: gpu=true.

charlie: That's the hyperparam sweep we kicked off last night. It should've had replica cap=4. Looks like the job ran with replicas=50 due to a config drift in the template.

dave: If it's low-priority we should preempt it. What's its priorityClass?

emma: It's using priorityClass `batch-low`. Serving has `serving-high`. Preemption should free nodes but autoscaler can't add nodes because cloud GPU quota is at max.

bob: Confirmed: cloud quota report shows GPUs in us-west2: quota=64, used=64. Node group can't grow.

alice: Options: 1) kill/scale down the runaway job, 2) evict non-critical pods, 3) move serving to a different pool/region if possible. Which is fastest?

charlie: Kill/scale down the job. I'll also follow up on why replica cap didn't apply.

dave: Can we taint the GPU pool to stop new scheduling while we clean up?

sre-oncall: Good idea. Taint to prevent more batch pods landing while we reconcile. Also prepare to cordon + drain if needed.

bob: Running: `kubectl scale job batch-train-2026-03-18 --replicas=2 -n ml`

bob: Scale command succeeded, pods scaling down.

emma: Applying taint: `kubectl taint nodes -l pool=us-west2-gpu-pool dedicated=infra:NoSchedule`

emma: Taint applied. New pods should avoid this pool.

charlie: There are still 4 pending pods that were already accepted by scheduler. Can we evict them?

dave: Deleting pending pods for that job to force restart elsewhere or stop them: `kubectl delete pod batch-train-2026-... -n ml --grace-period=0 --force` (iterating).

bob: Deleted 12 pending pods tied to the job. Autoscaler/cluster now reports 12 GPUs free but cloud API shows some node provisioning failures.

infra-bot: Autoscaler event: NodeGroup "gpu-us-west2-group" scaling attempt failed: quotaExceeded (requested: 4 GPUs, available: 0).

alice: So even though pods were removed, we can't get extra nodes due to provider quota. Need quota bump or shift region.

emma: us-east1 has capacity (20 free GPUs) but sending workloads cross-region will increase latency and egress costs for some customers. Not ideal for CAN/NA customers that require data to stay in region.

charlie: Short-term: keep serving on dedicated serving pool (no GPU shortage) by updating routing for canaries. Also ensure high-priority serving pods are scheduled on serving pool.

dave: Updated canary deployment annotation: `routing=serving-pool` -> will prefer nodes in serving-pool.

emma: Serving canaries are routing to serving-pool now. Latency metrics returning to baseline.

sre-oncall: Next steps (post-incident): 1) Add admission controller to enforce replica caps on batch jobs. 2) Alert when GPU quota > 90% earlier. 3) Runbook: how to taint/cordon/drain GPU pools safely. 4) Request emergency GPU quota bump with provider. 5) Give serving workloads preemptive priorityClass.

alice: I'll open a billing/cloud account ticket for quota increase and flag it as P1. Also creating infra issue for admission controller work.

bob: I'll add a CI check to ensure job templates include `spec.parallelism` caps and proper priorityClass.

emma: Note on cost: if we shift to us-east1 temporarily it will increase cross-region egress and might trigger extra dataplane costs. Documented in the incident ticket.

charlie: Action item: audit recent job template changes to find where the replica limit was dropped.

sre-oncall: Marking incident mitigated. Monitoring to confirm stable for 30m. Time: 1759012034.

alice: Thanks everyone. I'll start the postmortem doc and link runbook updates.

emma: Will follow up on routing and cost notes.

dave: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Incident automation: created ticket INFRA-4302 for quota request and INFRA-4303 for admission controller.

sre-oncall: Closing thread here; will post the full postmortem later.
